candidates.context: This guidance describes points to consider to ensure product quality and performance for MDIs 21 and DPIs. It describes chemistry, manufacturing, and controls (CMC) information recommended 22 for inclusion in new drug applications (NDAs) and abbreviated new drug applications (ANDAs); 23 however, the principles are applicable to products used during clinical trials, and over the 24 product lifecycle as well. It also provides recommendations on certain aspects of labeling for 25 NDA and ANDA MDI and DPI products. 26 FDA previously published a draft guidance on this topic on November 13, 1998. 2 The present 37 guidance is a revision of the previous draft, updated to reflect current standards and requirements 38

candidates.statement: Prior to the development of an MDI or DPI, the applicant should establish the desired quality 135 target product profile (QTPP). The QTPP is a prospective summary of the quality characteristics 136 of a drug product, and in this case, the combination product, that ideally will be achieved to 137 ensure the desired quality, taking into account safety and efficacy of the MDI or DPI (ICH 138 Q8(R2)). 9 Examples of QTPP elements for MDIs and DPIs include: proposed dosage form and 139 delivery system, strength (e.g., targeted metered dose for DPIs, targeted delivered dose for 140 MDIs), purity, stability, and aerodynamic performance. 141

candidates.statement: Early in the development process of an MDI or DPI, the applicant should develop a list of 147 potential CQAs for the combination product. A CQA is a physical, chemical, biological, or 148 microbiological property or characteristic that should be within an appropriate limit, range, or 149 distribution to ensure the desired product quality (ICH Q8(R2)). Those aspects of the design of 150 the combination product that are essential for proper functioning of the product are also 151 considered part of the required design output (21 CFR 820.30(d)). Knowledge of the QTPP for 152 the product, in combination with information from prior knowledge, risk assessments, and/or 153 experimentation, can be used to develop the list of product CQAs. candidates.statement: The materials used to fabricate the MDI device constituent part may come into direct contact 232 with either the formulation or the patient, thereby potentially affecting product safety and 233 performance. For example, due to the presence of organic propellant/vehicle in MDI 234 formulations, leaching of compounds from the valve and/or canister components of the container 235 closure system into the formulation can occur, which is a potential safety or effectiveness 236 concern. Device constituent part materials also have the potential to affect the aerodynamic 237 performance of the MDI product. For example, delivered dose and APSD of the MDI product 238 can be affected by the surface properties of the device constituent part and/or its components. 239 Therefore, the properties of materials used in the fabrication of the device constituent part and 240 the quantitative compositions after fabrication should be considered CQAs. 241

candidates.statement: The crystallinity of the drug substance in MDIs and DPIs can be affected by mechanical 416 processing, including micronization. This can lead to the generation of amorphous particles that 417 are thermodynamically unstable, with a tendency to convert to a more stable crystalline state 418 with time. This recrystallization of micronized material could lead to uncontrolled particle 419 growth, thereby affecting the MDI or DPI product CQAs (e.g., APSD, DDU). Therefore, a 420 conditioning step should be considered following micronization to allow conversion of 421 amorphous to crystalline form under controlled conditions of temperature and humidity. 422
